about: Lot 316 (external bug hunt, edition 1.4: BUG-106, BUG-89, BUG-96, BUG-86, N4): a security tool switched off by its system tools' other spellings, each from a cron job's own shell (no administrator's session, no coalescing) — systemctl's valued option before the verb (`-P Id`), a cluster ending in one (`-qs KILL`), an option after the verb (`--user`: a unit under POSIXLY_CORRECT), the agent's unit and auditd in one command (auditd named), an option no table holds (the reader's over-approximation, said in the record); iptables' long `--policy`, the multi-call binary's `main4 -F`, nft's command line in one argument, firewall-cmd's separate `--set-default-zone trusted`; pkill's `-n` and killall's `-g` (no value); a cloud agent's uninstaller run by a shell (NN-L-EVA-002, not its tool's process starting). Then an administrator's benign `systemctl status`, an iptables LOG rule whose prefix starts with `-F`, `nft list ruleset`, firewall-cmd's default zone `public`: nothing.

the kill of the ransomware actor's process tree (NN-L-IMP-001, lab PR 225)
the kill of the staged program that asked a security tool off (NN-L-EVA, lab PR 225)
the kill for a rename seen only as a watched directory's new entry (NN-L-FIM-010, a match added by lab PR 225)
the kill of a process that connected to a public address its lineage did not resolve (NN-L-NET-028, lot 275)
the kill of a runc outside the system directories — a container runtime's bundled runc (R013, lot 283b)
the kill of a cron entry's writer, after the write (NN-L-FIM-007, lot 283b)
the kill of a systemd unit's writer, after the write (NN-L-FIM-009, lot 283b)
